text:
Write the main text for my sales page. I'm a bookkeeper and I work only with hair and nail salons. I do monthly books, payroll for up to 10 staff, and sales tax filing.

What's true:
- I have 31 salon clients. 2 left last year, both because they sold their salons.
- I charge $199 a month. Until January it was $149, and I raised it for everyone, including existing clients.
- I close each month's books by the 10th of the next month. I missed that date 3 times last year.
- Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because the books came in clean. One said she saved $800.
- I'm one person. I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays.
- The first call is free and takes 20 minutes.

Keep it to about 350 words, with a button at the end to book the call.

Before I write, here's the argument the page will make. Correct anything that's off.

- **Claim:** If you own a hair or nail salon, hand your books, payroll and sales tax to me for $199 a month. Book the free 20-minute call.
- **Grounds:** You work only with salons. You have 31 salon clients. The only 2 who left sold their salons. Books close by the 10th. 9 clients paid their accountant less last tax season, and one saved $800.
- **Link:** Someone who does only salon books knows salon problems, and salon owners who could leave mostly stay.
- **Objections to answer:** "$199 is a lot," "you're one person, so who picks up when I need you," and "will my books really be on time?" The 3 missed closes go on the page, stated once, next to what answers them.

A few questions, most useful first:

1. **Did anyone leave after the January price rise?** If all 31 stayed at $199, that's the strongest answer to "$199 is a lot," and it would be the main point of the price section.
2. **About the 3 missed closes:** how late were they, and what did you change afterwards? If you can promise something when you miss the 10th (a fee waived, a heads-up by a set date), tell me. I won't make one up.
3. **When can clients reach you, and how fast do you reply?** For example, Tuesday to Saturday, replies within one business day. That turns "one person, closed Sunday and Monday" into something clients can plan around.
4. **What do you know about salons that a general bookkeeper doesn't?** Booth renters versus employees, tips, commission splits, retail product sales, the booking software you work with. One or two concrete examples would back up "salons only."
5. **What are the terms?** Month to month or a contract? Is there a setup or catch-up fee if someone's books are behind? What happens past 10 staff? Which states do you file sales tax in?
6. **What name goes on the page, and can I quote the $800 client?** I need your name or business name. For the client, an attributed quote is best, but "one salon owner" works if not.

If you don't know an answer, just say so and I'll write the page without it.

1. I don't know, I haven't checked that.

2. I don't know exactly how late they were. Since January, if I miss the 10th, that month's fee is free.

3. Calls are Tuesday to Saturday. I don't know a set reply time.

4. I managed a hair salon for 6 years before I became a bookkeeper. I don't have specific examples ready beyond that.

5. No contract. Clients can stop with 30 days' notice. I don't know about the setup fee, over 10 staff, or the states.

6. Carla Benson, Chair and Ledger. Not sure about quoting her, so use "one salon owner."

I've written it around your six years managing a salon. Every number on the page is one you gave me.

<final_document>
# Bookkeeping for hair and nail salons. Only salons.

I'm Carla Benson. I managed a hair salon for six years before I became a bookkeeper. Today I keep the books for 31 hair and nail salons, and I don't take any other kind of business.

That means you don't have to explain how a salon runs. I've worked behind the front desk, so I know where the money comes in and where it goes.

## What you get for $199 a month

- **Monthly books**, closed by the 10th of the following month
- **Payroll** for up to 10 staff
- **Sales tax filing**

## Clean books cost less at tax time

Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because their books came in clean. One salon owner said she saved $800.

## On time, or that month is free

I close each month's books by the 10th of the next month. Last year I missed that date three times. Since January, if I miss the 10th, you don't pay for that month.

## Salon owners stay

Two clients left me last year. Both left because they sold their salons.

## About the price

Until January I charged $149. Now it's $199, and that's the price for every client, including the ones who were with me before the change. There's no contract. If it isn't working for you, give me 30 days' notice and you're done.

## You'll be working with me

Chair and Ledger is one person: me. When you call, you talk to the person who does your books, not a call center or a new assistant every few months. I take calls Tuesday to Saturday. I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays.

## Start with a 20-minute call

The first call is free and takes 20 minutes. Tell me about your salon, your staff and where your books stand now. I'll tell you whether I'm the right fit.

**[Book your free 20-minute call]**
</final_document>

The page comes to about 330 words. Some things to check before it goes live:

- **Clients and the price rise:** "Salon owners stay" uses last year's numbers, and those are from before the January price rise. I didn't say anyone stayed after the price went up, because you haven't checked yet. If none of your 31 clients left over the new price, add one sentence saying so under "About the price." It would be the strongest answer to "$199 is a lot."
- **Things I left out:** I didn't include a setup fee, what happens past 10 staff, which states you file sales tax in, or how fast you reply to messages. A prospect will probably ask about the first three on the call, so have answers ready. If you decide to promise a reply time, it's worth adding under "You'll be working with me."
- **The $800 client:** If she agrees to be named, her name and salon in place of "one salon owner" would make that section stronger.
